text:
maria: quick heads-up — on the 13B int8 bring-up we’re seeing a consistent priming regression on long-context conversational prompts (~10% ROUGE-L drop on our customer slices). cost saves look good (~28% token $), but quality hit is non-trivial. sharing slice summary below.

jake: yikes. is this for int8 only or hybrid routing too?

maria: int8 baseline vs fp16:
- short-turn chat (<=3 turns): quality ~ parity (±1%)
- long-turn chat (>=8 turns): ROUGE-L -10% / PPL +1.8x
- avg token cost delta: -28% vs fp16
- inferred cause: priming tokens not preserved well after quantized KV-cache ops (esp repeated system prompts).

sara: can you dump a repro prompt? curious if it’s priming length or repeating tokens pattern.

maria: repro snippet: ```
System: You are a helpful assistant.
User: long multipart doc... (6 paragraphs)
Assistant: summary...
User: follow-ups x5
```
Repeatable. with int8 the assistant starts dropping earlier context around follow-up 3-4.

tom: possible causes: smaller mantissa/rounding in attention scores, or k-v cache eviction / compaction being lossy in quant path. Did we run with stable-kv on this build?

maria: we used runtime v2.14 with stable_kv=false (default). I ran a quick trace — k-v cache entries look consistent count-wise but similarity scores for earlier tokens shift by ~0.02 mean.

nina: interesting — product asked for unit-econ tradeoffs. if we route long-context to fp16, what’s cost hit? Jake — ballpark?

jake: routing long-context to fp16 increases unit cost for those requests by ~3.5x, but long-context traffic is ~12% of overall requests in slice -> net platform cost ~ +22% for that slice. overall customer bill impact depends on mix; for high-value GTN customers might be ok.

maria: proposed mitigation options: 
1) keep int8 default for short-turns, route long-context priming_long -> fp16 (canary 5%).
2) try int8 with stable_kv=true + stricter kv-quantization thresholds (cheap infra experiment).
3) fallback hybrid: use int8 encoding but fp16 KV cache for priming tokens (engineering heavier).
4) delay int8 rollout for customers that use longform multi-turn until we close the gap.

sara: option 2 first — cheap experiment and might fix rounding accumulation. If not, option1 routing + small canary seems pragmatic.

jake: ops note — routing rule would be: route_by: "priming_len >= 512" -> model: 13B-fp16; else -> 13B-int8. canary: 5% for all customers, 20% for internal dev orgs.

maria: added quick eval plan: 1) run stable_kv=true on prod-like bench for 24h against slice (~50k requests) and measure ROUGE/PPL + token-cost. 2) if stable_kv reduces gap to <3% on long-turns, proceed with int8 rollout. 3) else implement routing rule and run 5% canary for 48h.

canary-bot: canary check created #CANARY-6812345678 — traffic splits: 5% global, 20% dev. health probes: latency, error-rate, rouge-l, kv-sim-delta.

tom: one additional ask — add a priming-specific cache priming_prefix_hash to preserve exact system prompt tokens (cheap heuristic) while still using int8 for generation. small code change but might give outsized wins.

nina: for product guidance: if we route, recommend messaging to GTN: "we're enabling lower-cost quantized models for interactive flows; for deeply multi-turn conversations we’ll use a higher-fidelity variant to preserve long-context quality."

amy-prod: sounds good to me. prioritize option2 + metrics in 48h, and prep routing playbook if experiment fails. can we add a short note for GTN materials with the numbers (cost saved vs potential quality delta) once we have experiment results?

maria: will run stable_kv experiment now. adding owners: @jake for routing config, @tom for priming_prefix change, @sara for eval dashboard. will post results in this thread.

jake: ack. I’ll draft the routing flag and canary template.

sara: prepping evaluation slices and dashboards — expect first run stats by +24h.

maria: thanks — off to run bench.
metadata: priming regression, int8 bringup, unit economics, routing vs fallback, canary plan
